definitions.def: not harmful or offensive in any way
to experience or suffer something, especially an injury or damage
to make up for something; to reduce or balance the effect of something bad
the quantity of matter that a body contains, often measured in kilograms
a person who does not have specialized knowledge or training in a subject

grammar_choice.en_template: The {{1:bigger/biggest}} someone is, the more damage they can do to themselves through even a relatively innocuous {{2:accident/accidentally}}.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 누군가가 클수록, 비교적 무해한 사고를 통해서도 그들이 자신에게 입힐 수 있는 피해가 더 커진다.
explain: The 비교급 ~, the 비교급 ~ 구문 → bigger(비교급).
전치사 through의 목적어 자리 → 명사 accident.

grammar_choice.en_template: Despite {{1:toddlers falling/toddlers to fall}} over and bumping themselves regularly, the injuries they sustain {{2:are/is}} rarely serious.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 아기들이 정기적으로 넘어지고 부딪히지만, 그들이 입는 부상은 거의 심각하지 않다.
explain: despite + 동명사(falling) — despite 뒤에는 명사/동명사, to부정사 불가.

grammar_choice.en_template: Their relatively thick bones in comparison to their mass {{1:mean/means}} they rarely build up enough energy, even at top speed, {{2:to do/doing}} themselves much damage.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그들의 질량에 비해 상대적으로 두꺼운 뼈는, 최고 속도에서도 자신에게 큰 피해를 줄 만큼의 에너지를 거의 축적하지 않는다는 것을 의미한다.
explain: enough ... to V(~할 만큼 충분한) 구문 → to do.

grammar_choice.en_template: Because of their increased mass ({{1:compounded/compounding}} by the fact that they are falling from a greater height and that their reactions may be slower), adults falling over will impact the ground with a {{2:much/very}} larger force.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 증가된 질량(더 높은 곳에서 떨어지고 반응이 더 느릴 수 있다는 사실로 인해 가중됨) 때문에, 넘어지는 어른은 훨씬 큰 힘으로 지면에 충격을 가하게 될 것이다.
explain: 비교급 larger 강조 → much(very는 비교급 강조 불가).

grammar_choice.en_template: The nonlinear relationship between mass and bone strength means {{1:that/what}} although their bones are thicker than a toddler's in absolute terms, they may not be relatively thick {{2:enough/too}} to compensate for the larger impact.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 질량과 뼈 강도 사이의 비선형 관계는, 그들의 뼈가 절대적인 면에서는 아기의 것보다 두껍지만, 증가된 질량으로 인한 더 큰 충격을 보완하기에 상대적으로 충분히 두껍지 않을 수 있다는 것을 의미한다.
explain: means 뒤 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 → that(의문사 what 불가).
thick enough to V(V할 만큼 충분히 두꺼운) 구문 → enough.

grammar_choice.en_template: The body mass index (BMI) can {{1:serve/serving}} as a convenient way for non-experts to {{2:examine/examining}} their health conditions in daily lives.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 체질량지수(BMI)는 비전문가들이 일상에서 자신의 건강 상태를 점검하는 편리한 방법으로 활용될 수 있다.
explain: for non-experts to V — to부정사 형태 → examine.

grammar_choice.en_template: For the same reasons, taller people {{1:have been found/was found}} to suffer more fall-related injuries ― like hip breaks ― {{2:than/as}} shorter people.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 같은 이유로, 키가 큰 사람들은 키가 작은 사람들보다 고관절 골절 같은 낙상 관련 부상을 더 많이 겪는 것으로 밝혀졌다.
explain: 주어 taller people(복수) + 과거~현재의 연구 결과 → 현재완료 수동 have been found.

jumble.answer: The bigger someone is, the more damage they can do to themselves through even a relatively innocuous accident.
Despite toddlers falling over and bumping themselves regularly, the injuries they sustain are rarely serious.
Their relatively thick bones in comparison to their mass mean they rarely build up enough energy, even at top speed, to do themselves much damage.

Because of their increased mass (compounded by the fact that they are falling from a greater height and that their reactions may be slower), adults falling over will impact the ground with a much larger force.

The nonlinear relationship between mass and bone strength means that although their bones are thicker than a toddler's in absolute terms, they may not be relatively thick enough to compensate for the larger impact caused by their increased mass.
The body mass index (BMI) can serve as a convenient way for non-experts to examine their health conditions in daily lives.
For the same reasons, taller people have been found to suffer more fall-related injuries ― like hip breaks ― than shorter people.
